title: Endeavour Leaves Plymouth — The Voyage Behind a New Pacific Map
content: Lieutenant James Cook's Endeavour sailed from Plymouth in August 1768 on a Royal Society-backed mission to observe the 1769 transit of Venus in Tahiti. After the observation, sealed Admiralty instructions sent the expedition searching for the supposed southern continent, Terra Australis. The voyage combined astronomy, navigation and natural-history collecting with British imperial expansion, later charting New Zealand and the east coast of Australia.
explanation: The date itself is a useful historical footnote: Cook's ship-time journal dates the departure 26 August, while Joseph Banks recorded the same sailing as 25 August under civil time. Different eighteenth-century timekeeping conventions explain the apparent contradiction.
